summary: Theorem7.2 fails for an admissible deterministic walk. Actual graph walks have stronger negative starts. Three further missing auxiliary hypotheses admit explicit counterexamples but occur in stronger valid application regimes.

problems.decisive_evidence: All prefix W4 inequalities hold; all conditional W3 events sure; X0=166 for arbitrary p>0 contradicts O(p). Family N3200k gives168k-2.

problems.correction: Strengthen initial margin to match effective drift or tie bad-step budget to epsilon; supply corrected stochastic proof and application.
problems.repair_verification: Deterministic margin and negative actual initial value checked; full revised stochastic theorem not certified.

independent_acceptance_review.coverage_scope_check: The original report distinguishes its 46-page text coverage and 31 viewed pages from incomplete stalk enumeration and external spectral/core-process inputs. Focused acceptance independently checks the four existing Problems, all decisive hypotheses, and the stronger conditions in the actual applications. No new whole-paper review or counterexample to the main graph-rank conclusions is asserted.

scientific_checks.independent_derivation: With C=delta=1, epsilon=1/100, N=3200, X_N=3168 and R=3101,...,3199, the deterministic backward walk has bad jumps+1 and all other jumps-1. W0 is met by deterministic G_t encoding X_t and membership. W1 is equality; W2 holds; W3(a) holds surely at good steps and through t in R otherwise, while W3(b) is vacuous as every X_t>0. For t<=3100 the bad prefix is0; for 3101<=t<=3199 it is t-3100<=t/32, and at N it is99<=100. Thus W4 holds surely for every p in(0,1), but X_0=166. For N=3200k the same construction gives168k-2>0; this excludes an asymptotic-N escape.
scientific_checks.actual_dependency_and_counterevidence: Source pages21-22 expose the transfer to delta=1/2 without a corresponding initial-margin transfer. Theorem7.2 is the robust tool used for Theorem1.12(A1)/(B1), but actual graph walks on pages28-29 and39 have a negative initial margin (A1 at most -N/8). The example refutes the stated technical theorem, not those rank conclusions.
scientific_checks.repair_limits: A strengthened initial bound or epsilon-dependent bad-step budget is necessary. A complete corrected stochastic proof and rounding are not certified.

scientific_checks.independent_derivation: Sixteen perfectly correlated fair Bernoulli coordinates, with f=sum on the entire Boolean cube, have each c_k=1; at t=8 the actual probability is1 whereas the printed bound is2exp(-2)<1. No independence is present in the source statement.
scientific_checks.dependency: Source page18 explicitly uses independent truncated Poisson variables; the broader auxiliary statement fails, but that application has the missing hypothesis.

scientific_checks.independent_derivation: The graphical sequence (k,1 repeated k times,0 repeated k^2-1 times) has n=k^2+k, sum d_i^2=n and total degree2k. Among (2k-1)!! pairings only k! are simple, so probability=2^k/binomial(2k,k) tends0. Page9 explicitly includes0 in natural numbers.
scientific_checks.dependency: Applications have minimum degree2 or the linear total-degree constraint T4 on page31. This counterexample does not meet those stronger conditions. No separate B2 failure is claimed.

scientific_checks.independent_derivation: For every even n, eta=1/4,E=all,d=n,A=B=J_n, a balanced half-plus/half-minus vector is in the kernel. The slice is deterministically all ones. Appending it as a column leaves rank1; symmetric augmentation with zero new diagonal has rank2 instead of required3. Failure probability1 contradicts O_eta(n^-1/2).
scientific_checks.dependency: The source statements assume d>=1 only, while Lemma8.5 requires d<=n/2. Actual graph applications have d=O(log n) and |E| linear, so a suitable restricted slice bound is available. Part8.4(b) is not separately refuted.
